title: Migrating from TypeScript 6 to TypeScript 7 knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should a production-oriented TypeScript project demonstrate?
options: Type annotations as a replacement for authorization and validation.
A working happy path without tests or documentation.
Secrets committed into client bundles for convenience.
Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
questions.answer_key: Explicit contracts, runtime validation, tests for failures, secure configuration and reproducible delivery steps.
questions.explanation: Production readiness requires runtime, security, testing and operational evidence beyond type checking.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Migrating from TypeScript 6 to TypeScript 7”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with reviewing deprecated compiler options and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with reviewing deprecated compiler options and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Reviewing deprecated compiler options”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Migrating from TypeScript 6 to TypeScript 7”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check adopting new defaults, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume validating editor, build, and tooling compatibility is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check adopting new defaults, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Adopting new defaults”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
